$comment: Scanner waiver registry — the recorded, maintainer-granted half of a TS-SEC hand-ruling.
WHY THIS FILE IS HERE AND NOT IN THE SKILL FOLDER. `security-scan.yml` runs on
`pull_request_target` so that the workflow, the scanner, and the rules all come from the
BASE ref: a pull request cannot change what runs against it. A waiver read out of PR
content would hand that property straight back — a PR could annotate its own High finding
down to Medium and turn the required `scan` check green, which is exactly the bypass the
job exists to deny. So the registry lives on `main`, is read from the trusted checkout,
and only a maintainer can add an entry. The cost is deliberate: granting a waiver is a
separate, reviewed act, and a skill's PR cannot grant its own.
WHAT A WAIVER DOES. It downgrades a High finding to Medium and prints it WITH the reason.
It never removes it. The finding stays on the reviewer's screen; it just stops being the
thing that holds the merge button. SPEC.md still governs — the scanner finds evidence; it
does not clear a skill, and a clean scan is not a pass.
WHAT A WAIVER CANNOT DO. `TS-SEC-01` (secrets), `TS-SEC-02` (hardcoded environment) and
`TS-SEC-12` (instruction-shaped text) are marked Never N/A. An entry naming one of them is
a configuration error and `scan_skill.py` exits 2 rather than honoring it. Those get
fixed, not waived.
HOW MATCHING WORKS. An entry matches on skill + check + file + the exact source line, with
runs of whitespace collapsed. Line numbers are deliberately NOT part of the key, so a
waiver survives code moving up or down the file. The line's TEXT is part of the key, so a
waiver does NOT survive the code itself changing — an edited sink is an unreviewed sink and
comes back as High until someone looks at it again. That is the intended behavior, not a
rough edge. `scan_skill.py` reports any entry that matched nothing, so stale rows surface
instead of rotting here.
FIELDS. skill, check, file, match, reason, granted (ISO date), granted-by (GitHub handle).
All required. `reason` is prose a reviewer reads, not a ticket number.
